assume.text: Draft 1 (2026-11-17). macOS 26, SwiftUI defaults: unified toolbar, menu bar for the commands, system accent. No playback in the first Mac version, so no bar marker yet. Inter stands in for SF Pro on the canvas.

playback.text:
Approved by the owner on 2026-11-24 (draft 1). Playback comes to the Mac in a later release; the GTK app's behaviour (SPEC.md, module playback), drawn the macOS 26 way.
1. The controls float as a glass capsule over the desk at the window's bottom, the sheet scrolling under it: Previous Bar, Play/Pause, Next Bar (plain glyphs, as in Apple's Music), time, position slider, length, "Bar 2 of 110", Volume, Song · Hits · Both.
2. Song · Hits · Both is the native segmented picker.
3. Volume: a popover above the button with two sliders, Song and Detected hits (70 % and 100 % at first, remembered per song).
4. A Controls menu between View and Window, named as in Apple's Music (its guide: Choose Controls > Shuffle): Play or Pause (Space, as in Music), Previous Bar (←), Next Bar (→) (Music steps songs with the same arrows), Go to the Start (⌥←, QuickTime Player's key for the beginning of a movie; MacBooks have no Home key, Stickler also takes Home as on Linux), then Song, Hits, Both with a checkmark.
5. The bar marker in the accent blue; a click on a bar jumps there.
6. The "saved" note (M7) moves up above the capsule while a song is open.
New text for po/: "Controls". Menu name and keys checked against Apple's support guides for Music and QuickTime Player (2026-11-24).
